evidenceFor: the write-gate release added after CP2: what it releases, the proof that it cannot release anything else, and the raw local-suite comparison it was landed against
whyThisExists: The dispatch's defect is 219,472 cells ALREADY WRITTEN. Fixing the two writer sites stops new ones and removes none of them: the write gate only ever moved a cell still reading `unaccounted`, and every measured cell reads `absent-verified`, which is in EARNED_CELL_KINDS and isPublishable. So the writers-only design filed in CP2 was insufficient on its own, and the dispatch's own stated post-apply outcome (every county's setback verdict turns refuse with a count) would have been false without this change. Recorded here because it is a change to what the PR ships, made after CP1 pre-registered its falsifiers.

theReleaseRule.addedBranch: prc.cell_state ->> 'kind' = 'absent-verified' AND (basis.method LIKE $4 OR basis.finding LIKE $5)
theReleaseRule.releasedSet: exactly the two buckets P-255's census measured, keyed on the census's own exported prefixes
theReleaseRule.findingPrefix: no ruled setback table exists for
theReleaseRule.prefixesReadAtSource: P:/doc_repo/scripts/setback-parcel-census.mjs:45-46 -- NO_TABLE_PREFIX = "no ruled setback table exists for "; ROUTER_METHOD_PREFIX = "setback-table-router". Copied character for character, and asserted equal in the lane's test (drift guard).
theReleaseRule.selfClosing: a rewritten cell is no longer absent-verified, so a second run cannot match it again (asserted)
theReleaseRule.mirror: setbackCellMayBeMoved(state) is the pure mirror of the WHERE clause; a drift test pins the SQL text, both parameterized LIKEs and the two prefix constants to it

whoElseCanWriteTheseSignatures.method: repo-wide grep over hauska-factory src/ for the two prefix strings and for each of the five setback rail keys
methodPrefixWriters: src/jobs/parcel-setback-cells.mjs (the router-miss writer, basis.method "setback-table-router.resolveSetbackForParcel") -- the only writer of this string
findingPrefixWriters: src/jobs/parcel-envelope-cells.mjs (its own noRuledTableCells, the SAME method and finding strings, lines ~368-371)
whoElseCanWriteTheseSignatures.theTrap: The no-table signature is NOT unique to this job. A second job writes the identical basis.
whoElseCanWriteTheseSignatures.whyItIsStillSafe: The second job writes it on its own rails -- maxHeightFt / maxLotCoveragePct / maxFootprintSqFt (its exported RAIL_KEYS) -- and never on the five setback rails. The release's WHERE clause matches whatever the batch names, and the batch only ever names SETBACK_RAIL_ALLOWLIST, enforced at write time by assertNoFalseAbsence. So the disjointness of the two rail sets is the real control.
whoElseCanWriteTheseSignatures.notTakenOnTrust: A test imports parcel-envelope-cells.mjs's own exported RAIL_KEYS and asserts the intersection with SETBACK_RAIL_ALLOWLIST is empty, so the two files cannot silently drift apart.
whoElseCanWriteTheseSignatures.fiveSetbackRailWriters: src/jobs/parcel-setback-cells.mjs is the only job in the repo that writes setbackFrontFt/setbackSideFt/setbackRearFt/setbackCornerFt/setbackRules (the other hits are the rail registry src/lib/parcel-record-engine/rail-keys.js, the row-creation default in ingest-existing.js, and a comment in publish-gate-sched.mjs)

guardsProvenAbleToFire.why: DEV_PROCESS: a gating indicator must be proven able to fire. Both new guards were exercised against a mutation that should trip them.
guardsProvenAbleToFire.disjointnessGuard: real overlap = []; with `setbackFrontFt` added to the other job's rail list the computed overlap = ["setbackFrontFt"] (the assertion fires)
guardsProvenAbleToFire.metacharacterGuard: real prefixes test false/false (no % or _); a crafted prefix containing % tests true (the assertion fires)
guardsProvenAbleToFire.howRun: node -e, importing both job modules and recomputing the two predicates over the real exports plus one mutation each
guardsProvenAbleToFire.notVacuous: the release itself is proven live, not just declared: the processCityPage test asserts the five params reach the real UPDATE and that the released cell is counted in cellsMoved (5), and a second direction asserts a foreign absent-verified cell moves nothing (0)

compositionWithP284.fact: P-284 landed in this same file while the lane was building (#158), adding per-county stage row counts from the UPDATE's RETURNING plus the companion INSERT.
compositionWithP284.whyItMatters: The gate release changes WHICH rows the UPDATE returns, so the two features meet in the stage record's cost basis. That is asserted, not assumed: a remediation run's released cells must appear in cellsMovedByCounty, or a cost record would claim a run that rewrote a county's false absences wrote nothing.
compositionWithP284.commentFixed: P-284's own doc comment described the gate as 'unaccounted-only', which this change makes stale; it now states the widened rule and keeps P-284's point (written, not offered, is the count that matters).
